protocol.name: Bitso
protocol.summary: Bitso is a leading, regulated LATAM-focused cryptocurrency platform and institutional liquidity clearinghouse that serves as a high-throughput stablecoin and cross-border settlement rail. It abstracts banking rail fragmentation across Latin America, allowing seamless, chain-agnostic digital asset movement and localized fiat conversion.
protocol.geography: Deeply embedded within major Latin American financial markets including Mexico (SPEI integration), Brazil (Pix integration), Argentina, and Colombia, alongside highly liquid international remittance corridors routing out of the United States.
protocol.constraints: Wnode must remain stateless and non-custodial. All Bitso interactions must be ephemeral, signed, executed, and cleared without retention. Under no circumstances does the compute mesh hold customer balances, manage direct internal escrow pools, or persist compliance metadata post-settlement verification.

integration.type: Stateless RESTful API and WebSocket payload routing integration utilizing secure cryptographic payload signatures, operating as a chain-agnostic stablecoin bridge and automated localized fiat clearing network.
data_flows: Wnode sovereign compute agents initiate Bitso settlement instructions for cross-border or merchant flows by dispatching cryptographically structured JSON bodies containing target bank routing, exchange directions, and webhook receipt URIs.
Stablecoin or fiat conversions are triggered via Bitso APIs and executed statelessly, leveraging real-time order books or institutional over-the-counter (OTC) quotes to swap assets instantly.
All transaction metadata is streamed, processed in RAM, and wiped after completion, with execution logs zeroized upon receipt of an absolute network confirmation signature.
security: Ephemeral signing keys for each settlement instruction, employing temporary hardware security module (HSM) session token isolation to sign discrete API commands.
No custody: Wnode never holds user funds or private keys, routing incoming customer-controlled transaction parameters directly to destination execution addresses.
Encrypted in-memory processing with zero data retention, ensuring all sensitive exchange info, payment fields, and corporate keys are unlinked and destroyed upon pipeline exit.

value_to_wnode.settlement: Enables automated, real-time cross-border and merchant settlement for distributed agents, removing multi-day wire delays from standard business-to-business processing loops.
value_to_wnode.corridors: Provides native access to vital Latin American banking corridors, instantly expanding Wnode's global payment footprint into high-growth, technology-forward emerging markets.
value_to_wnode.agnostic: Aligns with Wnode’s chain-agnostic, issuer-agnostic settlement model by allowing multi-chain stablecoins (e.g., USDC, USDT across Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon) to interface interchangeably with local fiat systems like Pix and SPEI.

value_to_bitso.volume: Drives continuous, non-cyclical transactional settlement volume through high-frequency, autonomous machine-to-machine exchange matching layers.
value_to_bitso.distribution: Expands Bitso's business distribution model directly into the machine-driven agent economy, bypassing traditional consumer-facing web frontends.
value_to_bitso.positioning: Establishes Bitso as the critical, infrastructure-level stablecoin-to-fiat rail inside advanced sovereign cloud compute frameworks and autonomous network topologies.

workflow_examples: An execution agent registers an inbound corporate payment contract, polls a live Bitso API endpoint to secure a low-slippage fiat-to-stablecoin price lock, routes the swap, and immediately delivers the settled digital asset to a verified merchant wallet address.

Multiple localized routing agents dynamically shift transaction volume across distinct Mexican, Brazilian, and Colombian banks by pooling resources through Bitso's shared regional liquidity layer, bypassing offline financial intermediaries.

drivers: Cross-border corridor volume generated by automated programmatic enterprise software leases.
Merchant settlement flows requiring instant translation from multi-chain digital assets to local fiat rails.
Stablecoin conversion fees captured through algorithmic market-making spreads and volume-based tier structures.
Automated agent-driven payment activity running continuously without human operational pauses.
